newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan takes delivery of two U.S. F-16 fighters.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan takes delivery of two U.S. F-16 fighters.

text.p: Taiwan on Monday took delivery of the first two of 150 F-16 fighter planes bought from the United States to strengthen its air defences, the defence ministry said on Tuesday.

The ministry had always been tightlipped about the timetable for the delivery of the F-16s, bought in a 1992 deal that angered arch rival China. It had only said that the delivery would begin "some time after April".

"The first two planes have arrived in (the southern military base of) Chiayi from Okinawa," a ministry spokesman told Reuters during a ceremony commissioning a squadron of domestically made fighters at an air force base in the central city of Taichung.
He declined to give details or say when Taiwan planned to receive the rest of the planes.
Local media had speculated widely that the planes would be delivered in batches from a U.S. military base in Okinawa starting in April.
Taiwan also expects to take delivery in May of the first of 60 Mirage fighters bought from France before Paris, acceding to Chinese pressure, agreed to stop arming the island.
Both the F-16s and the Mirages are expected to play vital roles in Nationalist-ruled Taiwan's air defences against China. The two sides split after a civil war in 1949.
China, which regards any advanced military sale to Taiwan by foreign powers as an encroachment on its own sovereignty, had protested vehemently against the F-16 and Mirage deals.

China held war games and missile tests near Taiwan before the island's first direct presidential election in March 1996 in what Beijing acknowledged was a warning to Taiwanese voters not to drop a pledge to reunify with the mainland.
